bio.topic: Enzymes as biological catalysts: the lock-and-key model

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a catalyst?
options: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
A substance that is used up to start a reaction
A substance that slows down a reaction
A product formed at the end of a reaction
questions.answer: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the catalyst at the end of the reaction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of which type of molecule?
questions.hint: They are long chains of amino acids folded into a shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What name is given to the part of an enzyme where the substrate binds?
questions.hint: It is the 'working' region of the enzyme.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What name is given to the molecule an enzyme acts on?
questions.hint: It goes into the enzyme before the reaction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In the lock-and-key model, which part is represented by the 'lock'?
questions.hint: The key fits into it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does each enzyme usually catalyse only one reaction?
options: Its active site has a shape complementary to only one substrate
It can only work once before it is used up
It is too large to fit other molecules
It only works in the stomach
questions.answer: Its active site has a shape complementary to only one substrate
questions.hint: Think about shape and fit.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is formed when a substrate binds to the active site of an enzyme?
questions.hint: Its name combines the two molecules involved.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens to an enzyme after the products are released?
options: It is unchanged and can be used again
It is broken down into amino acids
It becomes part of the product
questions.answer: It is unchanged and can be used again
questions.hint: Remember the definition of a catalyst.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Amylase breaks down starch. What is the product of this reaction?
questions.hint: It is a sugar made of two glucose units.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which word describes the shapes of an active site and its substrate?
questions.hint: They fit together like matching puzzle pieces.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An enzyme digests 6 g of starch in 3 minutes. Calculate the mean rate of digestion in g per minute.
questions.hint: Rate = amount ÷ time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Without a catalyst a reaction takes 240 s. With an enzyme it takes 30 s. How many times faster is the reaction with the enzyme?
questions.hint: Divide the slower time by the faster time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Protease enzymes break down proteins into:
questions.hint: Proteins are long chains of these units.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Describe the sequence of events, using the lock-and-key model, from a substrate meeting an enzyme to the release of products.
questions.hint: Use the terms substrate, active site, complex and products in order.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why lipase cannot break down starch.
questions.hint: Compare the shape of lipase's active site with the shape of starch.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Suggest why living cells need enzymes to carry out their reactions at body temperature.
questions.hint: Think about how fast reactions would be without them, and what high temperatures would do to cells.

bss.topic: Jânio Quadros, João Goulart e o golpe de 1964

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano Jânio Quadros renunciou à Presidência da República?
questions.hint: Ele ficou menos de sete meses no cargo, depois de tomar posse em janeiro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual objeto Jânio Quadros usou como símbolo de campanha, prometendo 'varrer a corrupção'?
questions.hint: É um objeto usado para limpar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem era o vice-presidente quando Jânio Quadros renunciou?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Onde estava João Goulart no momento da renúncia de Jânio?
questions.hint: Era uma viagem oficial a um país socialista da Ásia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que movimento, liderado a partir do Rio Grande do Sul, defendeu a posse de Jango em 1961?
questions.hint: O nome lembra o respeito à lei e à Constituição.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual solução foi adotada em 1961 para permitir a posse de Jango com poderes reduzidos?
questions.hint: Nesse sistema, o primeiro-ministro passa a ter grande parte do poder.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano um plebiscito fez o Brasil voltar ao presidencialismo?
questions.hint: Foi no início do ano seguinte ao de 1962.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como ficou conhecido o conjunto de reformas propostas por João Goulart, como a agrária e a educacional?
questions.hint: O nome indica que mexeriam na estrutura do país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas era uma das reformas de base defendidas por Jango?
questions.hint: Tinha relação com a distribuição de terras.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O comício de 13 de março de 1964, em que Jango defendeu as reformas de base, ficou conhecido como:
questions.hint: Aconteceu em frente a uma grande estação de trem no Rio de Janeiro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual manifestação, em São Paulo, reuniu setores conservadores contra o governo Jango em março de 1964?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que contexto internacional ocorreu o golpe de 1964?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem foi o primeiro presidente do regime militar após o golpe de 1964?
questions.hint: Era um marechal do Exército.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a renúncia de Jânio Quadros gerou uma crise política em 1961.
questions.hint: Pense na reação dos militares e de setores conservadores à posse do vice.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que as reformas de base provocaram oposição de alguns grupos da sociedade?
questions.hint: Pense em quem poderia perder terras ou poder com essas mudanças e no medo do comunismo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Analise dois fatores que contribuíram para o golpe de 1964.
questions.hint: Considere fatores internos (economia, política) e externos (contexto internacional).

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is a stakeholder?

Only the owners of a business
Only the customers of a business
questions.answer: Any person or group with an interest in a business
questions.hint: It is a broader group than just the people who own shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an internal stakeholder?
questions.hint: Internal stakeholders work inside or own the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an external stakeholder?
questions.hint: External stakeholders are outside the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What name is given to the owners of a limited company?
questions.hint: They own part of the company's shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the main objective of most shareholders?
options: High dividends and a rising share price
questions.answer: High dividends and a rising share price
questions.hint: Think about a return on their investment.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which objective is most likely for employees?
questions.hint: Think about what workers want from their job.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder is most interested in the business paying its bills on time?
questions.hint: They provide materials and want to be paid for them.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder group wants good-quality products at low prices?
questions.hint: They buy the products.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why is the government a stakeholder in businesses?
options: Businesses pay taxes and provide jobs
questions.answer: Businesses pay taxes and provide jobs
questions.hint: Think about what the economy gains from businesses.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business wants to cut costs by reducing wages. Which stakeholders are most likely to be in conflict?
questions.hint: One group gains from higher profit, the other loses income.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A factory plans to expand and work 24 hours a day. Which stakeholder is most likely to object?
questions.hint: Think about noise, traffic and pollution.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder lends money to a business and wants it repaid with interest?
questions.hint: These are financial institutions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Identify one internal and one external stakeholder of a supermarket and state one objective of each.
questions.hint: Choose one group inside the business and one outside, then think about what each wants.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain why a decision to move production abroad could cause conflict between stakeholders.
questions.hint: Consider who gains from lower costs and who might lose jobs or business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one way a business could reduce conflict between its stakeholders.
questions.hint: Think about communication, consultation or compromise.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A café owner wants to raise prices to increase profit. Discuss how this might affect two different stakeholders.
questions.hint: Consider customers and employees or shareholders, and give positive and negative effects.

chem.topic: Reacting masses, limiting reactants and percentage yield

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of carbon dioxide, CO₂. (Ar: C = 12, O = 16)
questions.hint: Add the Ar of each atom in the formula.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃. (Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.hint: There are three oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the number of moles in 4.4 g of CO₂. (Mr = 44)
questions.hint: Moles = mass ÷ Mr.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the Mr of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄. (Ar: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
questions.hint: Count two H, one S and four O.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of CaO produced from 50 g of CaCO₃. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56)
questions.hint: Find the moles of CaCO₃ first; the mole ratio is 1:1.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Calculate the mass of MgO formed from 12 g of Mg. (Ar: Mg = 24; Mr: MgO = 40)
questions.hint: The mole ratio of Mg to MgO is 2:2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Calculate the mass of CO₂ produced when 8 g of CH₄ burns completely. (Mr: CH₄ = 16, CO₂ = 44)
questions.hint: One mole of methane gives one mole of carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. How many moles of NH₃ can be made from 6 moles of H₂ (with excess N₂)?
questions.hint: Use the ratio 3 mol H₂ : 2 mol NH₃.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What name is given to the reactant that is completely used up and limits the amount of product?
questions.hint: It 'limits' the reaction.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 4 mol of H₂ react with 3 mol of O₂. Which reactant is limiting?
questions.hint: Work out how much O₂ is needed for 4 mol of H₂.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Fe + S → FeS. 5.6 g of Fe reacts with 4.0 g of S. Calculate the maximum mass of FeS formed. (Ar: Fe = 56, S = 32; Mr: FeS = 88)
questions.hint: Find the moles of each reactant and identify the limiting one.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. 0.2 mol of Mg is added to 0.3 mol of HCl. Calculate the number of moles of H₂ produced.
questions.hint: Check whether there is enough HCl for all the Mg.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 20 g, but only 15 g of product is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A student expected 8.0 g of product and collected 6.4 g. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Divide what was obtained by what was expected, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Give two reasons why the percentage yield of a reaction is usually less than 100%.
questions.hint: Think about the reaction not finishing, side reactions and losses during separation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why chemists often use one reactant in excess.
questions.hint: Think about making sure the more expensive reactant is completely used.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the main purpose of encryption?
options: To make data unreadable to anyone without the key
questions.answer: To make data unreadable to anyone without the key

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name for data before it has been encrypted?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name for data after it has been encrypted?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In symmetric encryption, how many keys are used to encrypt and decrypt a message?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In asymmetric encryption, which key is used to encrypt a message sent to Priya?
questions.hint: Think about which key anyone is allowed to know.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In asymmetric encryption, which key must be kept secret by its owner?

questions.q: Which statement about encryption is true?
options: It does not stop data being intercepted, but makes it meaningless
It stops data from ever being intercepted
It only works on wired networks
It removes the need for passwords
questions.answer: It does not stop data being intercepted, but makes it meaningless

questions.subject: comp

questions.subject: comp

It is too slow to use at all

questions.subject: comp

It does not need any keys
It is always faster than symmetric

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is a common reason that symmetric encryption is still widely used?
options: It is faster for encrypting large amounts of data
It needs no key at all
It cannot be broken by any method

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which process turns ciphertext back into plaintext?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A Caesar cipher with a shift of 2 gives the ciphertext JGNNQ. What is the plaintext?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State two differences between symmetric and asymmetric encryption.
questions.hint: Think about the number of keys and how they are shared.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why a message encrypted with someone's public key can be safely sent over the internet.
questions.hint: Who holds the key needed to decrypt it?

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: "the team".
questions.hint: It is a feminine noun starting with a vowel.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Fill in the gap with the passé composé: "Vous ___ le match à la télé ?" (voir)
questions.hint: Use the vous form of avoir and the irregular participle of voir.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Fill in the gap: "Samedi, j'ai joué ___ rugby."
questions.hint: With sports, use jouer à; rugby is masculine.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write 2–3 sentences in French about what you did last weekend. Use at least two different verbs in the passé composé with avoir.
questions.hint: Try j'ai joué, j'ai fait or j'ai regardé, and add a time expression.

geog.topic: Coastal deposition landforms: beaches, spits, bars and tombolos

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is coastal deposition?
options: The dropping of material carried by the sea
The wearing away of cliffs by waves
The breaking up of rocks by weather
The movement of the tide up the beach
questions.answer: The dropping of material carried by the sea
questions.hint: Think about what happens when waves lose energy.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Name the process that moves sediment along a coastline in a zigzag pattern.
questions.hint: It is driven by waves arriving at an angle.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which type of wave tends to build up beaches?
questions.hint: Its name suggests building something.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which statement describes a constructive wave?
options: High and frequent with a steep form
questions.hint: Material is carried up the beach and left there.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Name the long, narrow ridge of sand or shingle that is attached to the land at one end and extends out into the sea.
questions.hint: It often forms where the coastline changes direction.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: The end of a spit often curves round because of changing wind and wave direction. What is this curved end called?
questions.hint: It is also described as a hook.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which landform often develops in the sheltered, calm water behind a spit?
questions.hint: Fine mud settles where water is calm.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What name is given to a ridge of sediment that grows across a bay, joining two headlands?
questions.hint: It can trap water behind it.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the body of water trapped behind a bar called?
questions.hint: It is a shallow, enclosed area of water.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Name the ridge of sand or shingle that joins an island to the mainland.
questions.hint: It is a special type of spit or bar.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which condition encourages deposition?
options: Waves losing energy in sheltered water
questions.answer: Waves losing energy in sheltered water
questions.hint: Material is dropped when there is not enough energy to carry it.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which plant is especially important for stabilising coastal sand dunes in the UK?
questions.hint: Its long roots bind loose sand.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What are the youngest, smallest dunes nearest to the sea called?
questions.hint: They are at the very first stage of dune growth.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which statement about beach profiles is usually true?
options: Sand beaches are gently sloping; shingle beaches are steeper
Shingle beaches are gently sloping; sand beaches are steeper
questions.answer: Sand beaches are gently sloping; shingle beaches are steeper
questions.hint: Think about how easily water drains through larger pebbles.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Describe how a spit is formed. Use the terms longshore drift and deposition in your answer.
questions.hint: Start with the direction of sediment movement, then explain what happens when the coastline changes direction.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain how sand dunes develop over time and why vegetation is important in this process.
questions.hint: Think about how sand is trapped, how plants grow and how dunes become more stable inland.

hist.topic: Long-term effects of the peace settlement on the 1930s

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which peace treaty dealt with Germany at the end of the First World War?
questions.hint: It was signed in a famous palace near Paris.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.hint: It was the year after the armistice.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What name is given to Article 231, which made Germany accept blame for the war?
questions.hint: It is about blame, or guilt.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Many Germans called the treaty a "Diktat". What did they mean?
options: A peace forced on them without negotiation
questions.answer: A peace forced on them without negotiation
questions.hint: Germany was not invited to the discussions.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: The treaty limited the size of the German army to how many soldiers?
questions.hint: It was far smaller than the army of 1914.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which area of Germany, bordering France, was demilitarised by the treaty?
questions.hint: It is named after a major river.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did Germany suffer hyperinflation, making its money almost worthless?
questions.hint: It followed missed reparations payments and the occupation of an industrial area.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which German industrial region did French and Belgian troops occupy in 1923?
questions.hint: It was the centre of coal and steel production.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In the context of the 1930s, what does "revisionism" mean?
options: Wanting to change or overturn the peace settlement
questions.answer: Wanting to change or overturn the peace settlement
questions.hint: Think of the word "revise".

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did German troops re-enter the demilitarised Rhineland?
questions.hint: It was a few years after the Nazis took power, before the Anschluss.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What name is given to the union of Germany and Austria in 1938, which the treaty had forbidden?
questions.hint: It is a German word meaning "connection" or "joining".

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which German-speaking border area of Czechoslovakia did Germany demand in 1938?
questions.hint: It surrounded part of Czechoslovakia's western border.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which statement best explains how the treaty helped extremist parties?
options: They used anger at the treaty to win support
The treaty banned all political parties
The treaty made Germany very wealthy
The treaty gave extremists control of the army
questions.answer: They used anger at the treaty to win support
questions.hint: Think about national humiliation and promises to undo it.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which of these is another long-term cause of the Second World War, alongside the peace settlement?
questions.hint: Look for an event from the late 1920s and 1930s.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain two ways in which resentment of the Treaty of Versailles contributed to the rise of extremism in Germany.
questions.hint: Consider territory lost, the War Guilt Clause, reparations and the economic crises that followed.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: "The Treaty of Versailles was the main cause of the Second World War." How far do you agree? Give one argument for and one argument against.
questions.hint: Weigh the treaty against other factors such as the Depression, appeasement and the weakness of the League of Nations.

math.topic: Straight-line graphs and the equation y = mx + c

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the gradient of the line y = 3x + 5?
questions.hint: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the y-intercept of the line y = 2x − 7?
questions.hint: In y = mx + c, c is where the line crosses the y-axis.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the gradient of the line y = −4x + 1?
questions.hint: Look at the coefficient of x, including its sign.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which line is parallel to y = 2x + 1?
questions.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8).
questions.hint: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the gradient of the line through (−2, 5) and (2, −3).
questions.hint: Work out the change in y and the change in x carefully with the negatives.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Write the equation of the line with gradient 4 and y-intercept −3.
questions.hint: Use y = mx + c.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The line y = 5x − 2 passes through a point with x = 3. Find the y-coordinate.
questions.hint: Substitute x = 3 into the equation.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (k, 11) lies on the line y = 2x + 3. Find k.
questions.hint: Substitute y = 11 and solve for k.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the gradient of the line 2y = 6x + 8.
questions.hint: Rearrange into the form y = mx + c first.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the y-intercept of the line 3y − 6x = 12.
questions.hint: Make y the subject.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the equation of the line through (0, 2) and (4, 10).
questions.hint: One point gives you c straight away; then find the gradient.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the equation of the line through (1, 5) and (3, 9).
questions.hint: Find m first, then substitute one point to find c.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the x-coordinate where the line y = 3x − 12 crosses the x-axis.
questions.hint: On the x-axis, y = 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A straight line slopes downwards from left to right. What can you say about its gradient?
questions.hint: As x increases, what happens to y?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain how you can tell whether the lines y = 3x + 2 and 2y = 6x − 1 are parallel.
questions.hint: Rewrite both equations in the form y = mx + c and compare.

phys.topic: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy; efficiency

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which equation gives kinetic energy?
questions.hint: Kinetic energy depends on the square of speed.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Calculate the kinetic energy, in joules, of a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s.
questions.hint: Use Ek = ½mv²; square the speed first.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A car of mass 1000 kg travels at 20 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy in joules.
questions.hint: Square 20, multiply by 1000, then halve.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 5 kg box is lifted 2 m. Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy in joules. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
questions.hint: Use ΔEp = mgΔh.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 60 kg climber goes up 10 m. Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy in joules. (g = 10 N/kg)
questions.hint: Multiply mass, g and height.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the unit of energy?
questions.hint: It is named after a scientist and its symbol is a single letter.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which equation gives efficiency?
options: useful output energy ÷ total input energy
total input energy ÷ useful output energy
questions.answer: useful output energy ÷ total input energy
questions.hint: Efficiency can never be more than 1 (or 100%).

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A device has a total input of 200 J and a useful output of 50 J. What is its efficiency as a percentage?
questions.hint: Divide useful by total, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A motor transfers 360 J usefully from 400 J of input energy. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
questions.hint: Efficiency = useful ÷ total × 100.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A motor is 80% efficient. It is supplied with 500 J. How many joules are transferred usefully?
questions.hint: Find 80% of the input.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A ball is dropped from a height. Ignoring air resistance, which energy transfer happens as it falls?
questions.hint: Height decreases while speed increases.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 0.5 kg ball is dropped from 5 m. Ignoring air resistance, calculate its speed in m/s just before it hits the ground. (g = 10 N/kg)
questions.hint: Set mgΔh equal to ½mv² and solve for v.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: If the speed of an object doubles, by what factor does its kinetic energy increase?
questions.hint: Look at the v² in the equation.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: In most machines, how is wasted energy usually transferred?
options: As thermal energy to the surroundings
As extra kinetic energy of the output
As chemical energy stored in the machine
questions.answer: As thermal energy to the surroundings
questions.hint: Think about why machines get warm.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Give one way of reducing the energy wasted by friction between moving parts in a machine.
questions.hint: Think about what you might add between surfaces that rub.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain why no real machine can have an efficiency of 100%.
questions.hint: Consider friction, air resistance and heating of the surroundings.

psych.topic: Sampling: target populations, random, opportunity and volunteer sampling

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a target population?
options: The whole group a researcher wants to study and apply findings to
The participants who actually take part
The people who design the study
The people who drop out of a study
questions.answer: The whole group a researcher wants to study and apply findings to
questions.hint: Findings are meant to be generalised to this group.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is the name for the smaller group of people selected from the target population to take part in a study?
questions.hint: It should ideally represent the larger group.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which statement describes random sampling?
options: Every member of the target population has an equal chance of being selected
Participants choose to take part by responding to an advert
Whoever is available at the time is asked
Only people the researcher knows are chosen
questions.answer: Every member of the target population has an equal chance of being selected
questions.hint: Think of drawing names from a hat.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which statement describes opportunity sampling?
options: The researcher uses people who are available and willing at the time
Every person has an equal chance of selection
Participants put themselves forward after seeing an advert
Every fifth name on a list is selected
questions.answer: The researcher uses people who are available and willing at the time
questions.hint: It is about convenience.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which statement describes volunteer sampling?
options: Participants select themselves, for example by replying to an advert
The researcher picks names using a computer
Participants are chosen by their teachers
The researcher asks anyone passing by
questions.answer: Participants select themselves, for example by replying to an advert
questions.hint: It is sometimes called self-selected sampling.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A researcher puts the names of all 200 students in a year group into a hat and draws out 20. Name the sampling method.
questions.hint: Everyone had an equal chance.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A researcher asks students sitting in the school canteen at lunchtime to complete a questionnaire. Name the sampling method.
questions.hint: The researcher uses whoever happens to be there.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A researcher puts an advert on a noticeboard asking people to take part in a memory study. Name the sampling method.
questions.hint: Participants decide for themselves to take part.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What term describes how far the results from a sample can be applied to the wider target population?
questions.hint: Think of the word "general".

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a weakness of volunteer sampling?
options: Volunteers may share characteristics, such as being more motivated, so the sample is biased
It always takes many years to complete
questions.answer: Volunteers may share characteristics, such as being more motivated, so the sample is biased
questions.hint: Think about who is likely to respond to an advert.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a strength of opportunity sampling?
options: Every person has an equal chance of selection
questions.hint: Think about how easy it is to find participants.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a weakness of random sampling?
options: It can be hard to get a complete list of the target population
It is always biased towards volunteers
It only uses people the researcher knows
It cannot be used with large groups
questions.answer: It can be hard to get a complete list of the target population
questions.hint: Every member needs a chance of being picked.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A psychologist wants to study memory in all Year 10 students in a city. She tests 30 students from one school. What is the target population?
options: All Year 10 students in the city
questions.answer: All Year 10 students in the city
questions.hint: It is the group she wants her conclusions to apply to.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which sample is most likely to be representative of a target population?
options: A sample of the researcher's friends
A sample from one club only
questions.hint: Think about size and equal chances of selection.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Explain one strength and one weakness of opportunity sampling.
questions.hint: Think about convenience, and about whether the people available represent everyone.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A researcher wants to study the sleep habits of teenagers in a large town. Suggest a suitable sampling method and justify your choice, including one possible problem.
questions.hint: Consider how representative the sample would be and how practical the method is.

pt.topic: Orações reduzidas de infinitivo, gerúndio e particípio

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: O que caracteriza uma oração reduzida?
options: Não tem conectivo e o verbo está em forma nominal
questions.answer: Não tem conectivo e o verbo está em forma nominal
questions.hint: Pense no que "falta" nela em comparação com a oração desenvolvida.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Quais são as formas nominais do verbo?
questions.hint: São formas que não indicam tempo nem pessoa por si só.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Ao chegar em casa, tomei banho.", a oração reduzida está em que forma nominal?
questions.hint: Observe a terminação do verbo "chegar".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Terminada a prova, os alunos saíram.", a oração reduzida está em que forma nominal?
questions.hint: Observe a terminação em -ada.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Estudando bastante, você passará.", a oração reduzida está em que forma nominal?
questions.hint: Observe a terminação em -ndo.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a forma desenvolvida de "Ao chegar em casa, tomei banho."?
options: Quando cheguei em casa, tomei banho.
Embora chegasse em casa, tomei banho.
Para que chegasse em casa, tomei banho.
questions.answer: Quando cheguei em casa, tomei banho.
questions.hint: A ideia é de tempo; escolha a opção com conectivo temporal.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a forma desenvolvida de "Terminada a prova, os alunos saíram."?
options: Depois que a prova terminou, os alunos saíram.
Embora a prova terminasse, os alunos saíram.
Para que a prova terminasse, os alunos saíram.
Se a prova terminar, os alunos sairão.
questions.answer: Depois que a prova terminou, os alunos saíram.
questions.hint: Pense em qual fato aconteceu primeiro.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Estudando bastante, você passará.", que valor tem a oração reduzida?
questions.hint: Tente desenvolvê-la com "se".

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Saí cedo para não perder o ônibus.", que valor tem a oração reduzida de infinitivo?
questions.hint: Pergunte: com que objetivo eu saí cedo?

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Mesmo sendo tarde, ela telefonou.", que valor tem a oração reduzida de gerúndio?
questions.hint: A ação acontece apesar de algo.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Para desenvolver "Treinou muito para vencer.", que conectivo de finalidade você usaria antes de "vencesse"?
questions.hint: É uma locução com duas palavras que indica objetivo.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual frase NÃO contém oração reduzida?
options: Quando o sinal tocou, todos saíram.
Ao tocar o sinal, todos saíram.
questions.answer: Quando o sinal tocou, todos saíram.
questions.hint: Procure a frase com conectivo e verbo conjugado.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a forma reduzida de infinitivo de "É importante que você leia."?
questions.hint: O infinitivo termina em -r.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a forma desenvolvida de "Chegando o professor, a aula começou."?
options: Quando o professor chegou, a aula começou.
Embora o professor chegasse, a aula começou.
Para que o professor chegasse, a aula começou.
Caso o professor chegue, a aula começará.
questions.answer: Quando o professor chegou, a aula começou.
questions.hint: A oração indica o momento em que a aula começou.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Reescreva a frase desenvolvendo a oração reduzida e explique o valor dela: "Feito o acordo, as equipes voltaram ao trabalho."
questions.hint: Escolha um conectivo que mostre a ordem dos acontecimentos.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Crie uma frase com oração reduzida de gerúndio com valor de causa. Depois, escreva a mesma frase na forma desenvolvida.
questions.hint: Na forma desenvolvida, use um conectivo como "como" ou "porque".

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: A que momento do Modernismo brasileiro pertence a poesia de Carlos Drummond de Andrade?
options: Primeira geração (Geração de 22, sua fase mais radical)
questions.hint: Pense na década em que publicou seu primeiro livro.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual cidade natal do poeta, em Minas Gerais, aparece com frequência em sua obra?
questions.hint: É uma cidade mineira ligada à mineração de ferro.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: No eu lírico de Drummond, o que sugere a palavra "gauche"?
options: Alguém deslocado, desajeitado, que não se encaixa no mundo
questions.answer: Alguém deslocado, desajeitado, que não se encaixa no mundo
questions.hint: Em francês, a palavra quer dizer "esquerdo".

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual poema, que abre o primeiro livro do autor, apresenta um "anjo torto" e o destino gauche do eu lírico?
questions.hint: O título fala de faces e de um número.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual foi o primeiro livro de poemas de Drummond, publicado em 1930?
questions.hint: O título é modesto, como se fosse "um pouco" de poesia.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual recurso é mais marcante no poema "No meio do caminho"?
options: Rimas ricas em todos os versos
questions.hint: Pense no que o leitor percebe logo na primeira leitura.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: A pedra em "No meio do caminho" é frequentemente interpretada como:
options: Um obstáculo ou acontecimento marcante na vida
questions.answer: Um obstáculo ou acontecimento marcante na vida
questions.hint: Algo no meio do caminho atrapalha a passagem.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Por que "No meio do caminho" causou polêmica quando foi publicado?
options: Pela linguagem simples e repetitiva, que rompia com padrões tradicionais
Por ser escrito em outra língua
questions.answer: Pela linguagem simples e repetitiva, que rompia com padrões tradicionais
questions.hint: Lembre-se das propostas modernistas.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: No poema "José", o que expressa a pergunta repetida "E agora, José?"
options: Um impasse diante de uma situação sem saída
questions.answer: Um impasse diante de uma situação sem saída
questions.hint: Pense no que acontece quando tudo acaba para alguém.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Quem é José no poema de Drummond?
options: Um homem comum, anônimo, em crise
questions.answer: Um homem comum, anônimo, em crise
questions.hint: O nome é muito comum no Brasil.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual livro de 1945, marcado pela poesia social e pelo contexto da Segunda Guerra Mundial, é um dos mais importantes do autor?
questions.hint: O título junta uma flor e o povo.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: O que caracteriza a poesia social de Drummond?
options: A preocupação com o mundo, a guerra e as injustiças
O foco apenas em paisagens naturais
questions.answer: A preocupação com o mundo, a guerra e as injustiças
questions.hint: Pense no contexto histórico dos anos 1940.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Drummond usa com frequência o verso livre. O que isso significa?
options: Versos sem métrica e rima obrigatórias
Versos escritos em prosa sem pontuação
questions.answer: Versos sem métrica e rima obrigatórias
questions.hint: "Livre" de quê?

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Qual atitude é comum no eu lírico drummondiano?
options: A ironia, inclusive sobre si mesmo
A exaltação heroica de si mesmo
questions.answer: A ironia, inclusive sobre si mesmo
questions.hint: O eu lírico gauche não se leva tão a sério.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Explique o que é o eu lírico gauche na poesia de Drummond e por que ele é importante para entender sua obra.
questions.hint: Pense em deslocamento, timidez, ironia e na relação do eu com o mundo.

questions.subject: pt_lit
questions.q: Compare "No meio do caminho" e "José": que sentimento ou situação humana cada poema expressa, e que recursos o poeta usa?
questions.hint: Observe a repetição nos dois poemas e o tipo de dificuldade que cada um apresenta.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: O que é uma carta do leitor?
options: Um texto enviado por um leitor a um jornal ou revista comentando algo publicado
Uma carta pessoal para um amigo
questions.answer: Um texto enviado por um leitor a um jornal ou revista comentando algo publicado
questions.hint: O próprio nome indica quem escreve.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: Onde as cartas do leitor costumam ser publicadas?
options: Em uma seção própria de jornais, revistas ou sites de notícias
questions.answer: Em uma seção própria de jornais, revistas ou sites de notícias
questions.hint: Pense em um espaço reservado para a opinião do público.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: Qual é a principal finalidade de uma carta do leitor?
options: Opinar, elogiar, criticar ou sugerir sobre uma matéria
questions.answer: Opinar, elogiar, criticar ou sugerir sobre uma matéria
questions.hint: É um gênero de opinião.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: A quem a carta do leitor se dirige principalmente?
options: Aos editores do veículo e aos outros leitores
questions.answer: Aos editores do veículo e aos outros leitores
questions.hint: Ela é enviada a uma publicação e pode ser lida pelo público.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: Como costuma ser o tamanho de uma carta do leitor?
questions.hint: Os veículos têm espaço limitado.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: Qual registro de linguagem é mais adequado para uma carta do leitor?
questions.hint: A carta será lida por muitas pessoas.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: O que é importante aparecer logo no início de uma carta do leitor?
questions.hint: O leitor da publicação precisa saber do que se trata.

questions.subject: pt_red
questions.q: Qual frase de abertura é mais adequada para uma carta do leitor?
